body:
_Migrated from issue #1070, filed 2026-07-21._

An idea worth building: let people set a subtle animated backdrop for their library — something beautiful to open, rather than a flat panel.

**Shape.** A per-user setting, off by default, that puts a gentle looping ambient scene behind the library view (and likely the reader's side margins). Users can point it at their own image or short loop; we'd also ship a few curated scenes.

**Non-negotiables**, because this is the kind of feature that goes wrong quietly:
- Honours `prefers-reduced-motion`, plus an explicit reduce-motion toggle.
- Opacity/blur control, with WCAG 2.2 AA text contrast holding over *every frame* — not just the first one.
- A strict performance budget with a still-image fallback and pause-when-hidden, so a looping backdrop behind a scrolling grid stays smooth on a Raspberry Pi or an old tablet.
- Short muted looping video/WebP rather than GIF — much better quality per byte.
- Uploaded assets are user data: size caps, MIME validation, and the security-review gate on the upload path.

Design note first (modality matrix across mobile/desktop and light/dark, performance budget, a11y contract), then a vertical slice with one scene.

Filed from a maintainer idea; comments and opinions welcome, especially from anyone running on low-powered hardware.
title: Ambient animated backgrounds for the library and reader
